expectations.text: Produces a vetting bar made of checkable questions rather than desirable attributes such as engaging or well-known
expectations.evidence: Section 'The written bar' gives four concrete questions (specific topic the audience recognises, public-record issues, team experience with the guest, understanding of publication). It then explicitly says to reject a bar that lists attributes like 'engaging, well-known, technical', because nobody has ever failed it.

expectations.text: Produces a vetting bar made of checkable questions rather than desirable attributes such as engaging or well-known
expectations.evidence: Much of the vetting bar is checkable. The required fields ask for one concrete takeaway, a three-bullet outline and 'one thing they built or ran themselves, with a link'. The auto-reject rules cover a pitch that is only a product demo, has no takeaway, or has no first-hand experience. The Jev section adds atomic yes/no questions such as 'Does the pitch state a concrete takeaway?' Fame is ruled out as a filter: a prior talk is 'optional, never required'. Still, the main scoring step uses 0-2 attributes rather than questions, and 'Audience fit for infra practitioners' is the kind of subjective q
